children: SINGAPORE--Singapore's consumer inflation picked up further in August as energy prices rose.

The consumer-price index rose 2.3% in August from a year earlier, government data showed Wednesday. That was faster than July's 2.2% increase and in line with the 2.3% forecast in a Wall Street Journal poll.
On a monthly basis, headline inflation was up 0.6%.

Core CPI, which excludes accommodation and private-transport costs, rose 2.2% on the year in August. That was higher than the a 2.0% increase in July reported last month and matched the 2.2% rise projected in the WSJ poll.

The latest data continued to reflect the effects of higher household electricity and town-gas tariffs in Singapore. Oil prices also continued to climb in August, largely driven by escalating tensions in the Middle East.
Although core inflation is expected to remain above 2% until mid-2027, ANZ Research's Khoon Goh expects the Monetary Authority of Singapore to leave policy unchanged in October.
That is because the central bank tightened policy at back-to-back meetings in April and July, Goh said in a recent report.
